title: a head-on pair: the alert at 4 x max(r), AVOID_COLLISION with its entry values the next tick, and the exit back to FLY_TO_DESTINATION
derivation: Self (radius 40, flying at maxFlightSpeed 320 with desired speed 320) is in FLY_TO_DESTINATION toward (0, 0, 20000), dead ahead, so its sticks stay 0 and its path is the +z axis. FLY_TO_DESTINATION calls avoidCollision when an alert exists (ShipEntity.m:5131-5133); IDLE has no such call site (3708-3722), so the fixture does not use it. A second ship (id 102, radius 40, mass 20000) starts at z = 6001 on the same axis facing -z at 320 m/s (constant-velocity), so each tick both move 2.666667 m and the centre distance is 6001 - 5.333333 k (the body advances in (a) before self's update, self's tick-k position is 2.666667 k). The pair trigger needs the centre distance below 4 x max(r) = 160 m with a strict < (CollisionRegion.m:299, 309, PROXIMITY_WARN_DISTANCE 4); the zone of setProximityAlert: is (2 x 40 + 40)^2 = 120^2 with the forward component multiplied by 0.25 at full speed (6124-6131), so the zone reaches 480 m ahead and the pair trigger decides. The first tick whose end satisfies it is k = 1096 (distance 155.667 m; at k = 1095 it is 161.000 m, a margin of 1 m). The alert is read by the next update: at tick 1097 FLY_TO_DESTINATION calls avoidCollision, which saves behaviour, target, desired range, desired speed and destination, sets destination to the midpoint of self's position (its tick-1096 position, self has not moved yet in that update) and the body's tick-1097 position, desired_range 10 x 40 = 400, behaviour AVOID_COLLISION and pitching_over (5919-5934). From tick 1098 behaviour_avoid_collision sets destination to the other ship's position and desired_range 400 every tick while the alert holds (5161-5165), tracks away from it with trackDestination (retreat) and sets desired_speed = maxFlightSpeed * (0.5 dq + 0.5), dq = d_forward squared = 1 here (5166-5169). At the alert distance of 4 x max(r) = 160 m and a closing speed of 640 m/s a faithful port may still pass through the other hull (the minimum centre distance over this run is 2.03 m, recorded as observed), so the fixture checks the alert, the entry values and the exit, not a clearance. The alert clears at tick 1148 and the behaviour resumes at tick 1255: those two ticks come from the reference replay (discrete fields, identical in float32 and float64), and the restored values are the saved ones (5943-5955). Closed forms for the rest.

title: a parallel-offset pass at a lateral offset of 100 m (2.5 r) alerts, enters AVOID_COLLISION and resumes
derivation: Self flies FLY_TO_DESTINATION at full speed toward (0, 0, 60000) on its own track (sticks 0, a straight line until the alert; IDLE has no proximity call site and would never enter AVOID_COLLISION). The other body (id 102, radius 40, mass 20000) moves at 320 m/s on the antiparallel track x = 100, a lateral offset L = 100 m. setProximityAlert: alerts only when d2 <= (2 r_self + r_other)^2 = 14400 (ShipEntity.m:6119-6131; the forward stretch 0.25 x max / speed scales only the forward component, so the lateral offset is a lower bound on the zone distance) and the pair trigger needs the centre distance below 4 x max(r) = 160 with a strict < (CollisionRegion.m:304-309, PROXIMITY_WARN_DISTANCE 4 in Universe.h:98-99). L must therefore lie strictly between r1 + r2 = 80 and min(2 r_self + r_other, 4 max(r)) = 120: for equal radii r that is 2.5 r = 100, strictly between 2 r = 80 and 3 r = 120; the numbers for the radii used are L = 100, 80 < 100 < 120. With forward separation f(k) = 6001 - 5.333333 k the pair trigger f^2 + L^2 < 160^2 means f < 124.900 and the zone (0.25 f)^2 + L^2 <= 120^2 means f <= 265.330, so the pair trigger decides; the first tick whose end satisfies both is k = 1102 (f = 123.667 m, one tick earlier 129.000 m). At tick 1103 avoidCollision runs: AVOID_COLLISION with destination the midpoint of self's tick-1102 position (0, 0, 2938.667) and the body's tick-1103 position (100, 0, 3059.667), desired_range 400, pitching_over 1 (5919-5934). At tick 1104 the destination is the body's position (5162-5165). The clearance is not promised: the minimum centre distance over the reference's run is 100.01 m at tick 1126, recorded as observed (it never goes below r1 + r2 = 80 here). The alert clears at tick 1140 and the behaviour resumes at tick 1274, both from the reference replay as discrete fields. Closed forms for the rest.

title: the same pass at a lateral offset of 2 (r1 + r2) = 160 m never alerts
derivation: The parallel-offset pass again, with the lateral offset L = 2 x (r1 + r2) = 160 m. The centre distance is sqrt(f^2 + L^2) >= L = 160 at every tick, and the pair trigger needs a distance strictly below 4 x max(r) = 160 (CollisionRegion.m:309), so it can never fire; the zone 2 x r_self + r_other = 120 is also smaller than L, so setProximityAlert: could not alert either (ShipEntity.m:6126-6131). The forward separation f(k) = 6001 - 5.333333 k is never exactly 0 at a tick (the tick nearest abeam is k = 1125, f = 1.000 m), so L^2 + f^2 > 160^2 at every tick, and the check is robust in both widths. proximityAlert is 0 and behaviour FLY_TO_DESTINATION at the abeam tick, before, after and at the horizon, with an empty events list. The self-test additionally replays every tick and asserts no alert.

title: a station dead ahead at full speed alerts at its 2,000 m pair trigger, with a planet body placed as Oolite places the station's planet
derivation: A station (id 2, scan class CLASS_STATION, radius 500, mass 1e7) is dead ahead of self at (0, 0, 6001), self flying at full speed (flightSpeed = maxFlightSpeed 320). The station is a ship in Oolite's collision pass; setProximityAlert: ignores nothing here (other mass above 2000, self is not a station, self is crewed and neither launching nor docking, ShipEntity.m:6105-6117). Pose conditions: at full speed the forward stretch is 0.25 (6124-6125), so the zone reaches 4 x (2 x 40 + 500) = 2320 m ahead, more than the pair trigger, and the pair trigger at 4 x 500 = 2000 m (strict <, CollisionRegion.m:309) decides; at a lower speed the zone would shrink and a station 2000 m ahead might not alert. Prefilter condition: Oolite tests a pair only when each entity's +-2 x collision-radius interval overlaps another collidable entity's on every axis (Universe.m:6713-6760, 7045-7073; entities left alone on an axis are skipped at CollisionRegion.m:243-248), which for an isolated station-and-ship pair is |delta| < 2 x (500 + 40) = 1,080 m per axis, so a two-body fixture would not be Oolite's truth at 2,000 m. The planet collides (Entity.m:825-828; OOPlanetEntity does not override canCollide) and its collision radius is the planet radius (OOPlanetEntity.m:119-120), and Oolite puts the main station 2R from the planet centre (Universe.m:1541-1547). The planet body (id 1, radius R = 41160, the Lave planet radius) is therefore placed at the station plus 2R along the unit vector (0.6, 0.64, 0.48), whose components all lie below 0.8 in magnitude: its centre is (49392.0, 52684.8, 45514.6). Self's and the station's +-2 x radius intervals lie inside the planet's +-2R = +-82320 interval on every axis for the whole horizon (the self-test asserts it at every replayed tick from this fixture's own coordinates), so every entity is chained and the plain pair trigger is Oolite's rule. The planet is never an alert candidate: it is not a ship (CollisionRegion.m:308-310), so reference rule (d) skips it. The first tick whose end is below 2000 m is k = 1501 (distance 1998.333 m; one tick earlier 2001.000 m). Entry values at tick 1502: AVOID_COLLISION, destination the midpoint of self's tick-1501 position and the station, desired_range 10 x 500 = 5000, pitching_over 1; at tick 1503 the destination is the station's position. Closed forms.

title: a light ship below 2000 kg dead ahead never raises an alert
derivation: A static ship (id 102, radius 40, mass 1000) at (0, 0, 700) dead ahead of self at full speed.
